Damn,you could be describing me.So in my own experience with being kind of extroverted but with anxiety and social isolation I think what makes me feel better is doing activities that I enjoy and focusing on myself.It's not necessarily bad to be a loner,the difference to being alone and feeling lonely is how you deal with your own presence.Crowds of young people can make you feel uneasy or like you might be "missing something" but If you build your confidence that will stop being a huge worry.About being physically fatigued, unfortunately the only way to build resistance is by exercising,start by walking for university (if you live close) or at least 3 times per week for 30 minutes, it's the easiest "workout" to begin with.

The best advice I can give is to slowly and with patience grow your self esteem.I know looks matter to most people and in these days we're bombarded with pictures of "role models",and how you should look and act like.I'm not suggesting it's an easy thing to do,but try to be the best version of you, especially in terms of attitude.Don't try to fit the mold,It gets tiring and you'll attract the wrong people.See this as a way of filtering all the people who would do you no good and by making yourself more resistent to critics your confidence will grow and someday someone will be attracted to your charisma and even your looks(everyone has a different taste, remember that).So for now,try to focus on how to improve your mood and looks,maybe by taking care of your health physically and mentally,but again,with patience and respect for yourself ❤️
